 View image in fullscreen ‘Our voices, our journey’: 2026 Taiwan Pride parade – in pictures 
 An estimated 150,000 people took to the streets of Taipei on Saturday to attend the 24th Taiwan LGBT+ Pride parade. The largest annual pride event in east Asia, the march aims to promote gender equality, foster cross-community dialogue, and advocate for expanded legal protections and social inclusivity
 ‘We’re not freaks’: police raid sparks concern for Taiwan’s LGBT-friendly image 
 Participants march through the streets during the annual Taiwan LGBT+ Pride parade in Taipei. Photograph: Cheng Yu-Chen/AFP/Getty Images Sat 31 Oct 2026 22.13 EDT Last modified on Sun 1 Nov 2026 00.44 EDT Share View image in fullscreen Participants wave flags and shout ‘Our voices, our journey’, the march’s 2026 slogan. Photograph: Ritchie B Tongo/EPA Share View image in fullscreen This year’s theme urges the public to combat political polarisation and global anti-DEI backlash through active listening and solidarity. Photograph: Chiang Ying-ying/AP Share View image in fullscreen The parade route wound through the streets of central Taipei, starting and finishing at the city hall. Photograph: Cheng Yu-Chen/AFP/Getty Images Share View image in fullscreen Representatives from Gilead Sciences lead their corporate contingent during the 24th Taiwan LGBT+ Pride parade. Photograph: Cheng Chia Huang/Getty Images Share View image in fullscreen A police raid on a Taipei gay bar in October was criticised by rights groups as heavy-handed, with some local campaigners alleging longstanding institutional homophobia from police. Photograph: Chiang Ying-ying/AP Share View image in fullscreen Other LGBTQ+ venues in Taiwan have also faced pressure, with a gay bathhouse closing in April after police raids and inspections. Photograph: Cheng Yu-Chen/AFP/Getty Images Share View image in fullscreen Taiwan legalised same-sex marriage in 2019, the first place in Asia to do so. Photograph: Cheng Yu-Chen/AFP/Getty Images Share View image in fullscreen A recent survey that found public support for marriage equality has increased from 42% to 54% since being made law. Photograph: Chiang Ying-ying/AP Share View image in fullscreen Participants carry a giant rainbow flag through the streets as part of the annual Taiwan LGBT LGBT+ Pride parade. Photograph: Chiang Ying-ying/AP Share View image in fullscreen A festival attender helps carry the giant rainbow flag through the streets. Photograph: Ritchie B Tongo/EPA Share View image in fullscreen Participants were not deterred by scattered cloud and a brief afternoon shower. Photograph: Tsai Hsin-Han/Reuters Share View image in fullscreen People wave rainbow flags and accessories during the annual Taiwan LGBT+ Pride parade.
